A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same spatial/contextual node-embedding framework, renamed from ClassContrast to SCNode. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification, link-prediction, GNN-integration, and feature-ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds benchmark evaluations and training-size, neighborhood-size, and similarity-metric analyses.

M1.justification: The spatial class histograms, contextual class-landmark features, concatenation, iterative transductive predictions, and link-prediction procedure are retained. Renaming and expanded explanations do not establish a new method component; classifier configuration changes are assessed under E3.

E1.justification: v2 Table 3 adds evaluated coverage on Amazon-Ratings, Tolokers, and Questions. It also reports filtered Squirrel and Chameleon evaluations, while the original unfiltered Squirrel evaluation disappears. The downstream tasks remain node classification and link prediction. Roman-Empire appears in dataset statistics without reported evaluation outcomes.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds ACM-GCN, Ordered-GNN, TEDGCN, and FGSAM-SAGE while removing ALT-APPNP. OGB comparisons add S3GCL and LMSPS, and link prediction adds HAGNN. The additional heterophilic comparison includes new comparator families such as NodeFormer, GraphGPS, SGFormer, and Polynormer.

E3.justification: The reported classification configuration changes from 700 hidden neurons to a single 100-neuron hidden layer, with L2 regularization changing from 0.00001 to 0.0001. GNN integration changes its stated learning rate from 0.05 to 0.001. New experiments introduce additional benchmark splits, neighborhood/metric controls, and training fractions of 5–75% with a fixed 20% test set.

E4.justification: v2 adds a limited-supervision study in Figure 5 and neighborhood-size and contextual-metric sensitivity studies in Appendix B.4, including accuracy/runtime tradeoffs. Conversely, v1's Squirrel homophily matrices and associated failure analysis are removed. The original spatial-versus-contextual ablation remains.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 10 runs for the established small-benchmark protocol and retain the same plus/minus reporting convention. Additional result rows do not introduce a new uncertainty estimator, seed-reporting practice, confidence interval, or significance test.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises several reported scores, including CITESEER from 86.86 to 77.83 and Texas from 90.54 to 94.59; changed stated configurations prevent interpreting these as identical-setting performance changes. Integration results, ablation values, and convergence curves also change, alongside substantial new benchmark and sensitivity results. The proposed method's OGB and link-prediction scores are retained.

T1.justification: The homophily definitions, main homophily theorem, and appendix proofs are retained after renumbering. New Remark A.5 adds the representation alpha_k = P_k(A)Y and a spectral/expressivity argument claiming that contextual coordinates enlarge the representable function class. This is additional mathematical reasoning, rather than a replacement of the existing theory.

C1.justification: The principal contribution is recast from a physics-inspired application of Energy Landscape Theory to class-relative spatial/contextual coordinates. v2 explicitly claims mitigation of the 1-WL locality bottleneck and general plug-and-play applicability to any GNN. The underlying claims concerning homophily matrices and predictive usefulness remain.

C2.justification: Energy-landscape and structural-balance explanations are replaced by landmark-coordinate and spectral interpretations. v2 adds explanations involving labeled representatives, limited supervision, and neighborhood/metric tradeoffs. It retains landmark-quality dependence but removes the explicit computational-overhead limitation for extremely large or high-dimensional graphs and proposes future landmark-selection remedies.

D1.justification: The anonymous code address is replaced by a named GitHub repository reference. v2 specifies a single hidden layer, revises documented hyperparameters, clarifies fixed training-derived prototypes, and supplies timings for new ablations. Hardware and most dataset-specific embedding recipes remain unchanged; the original Squirrel-specific details are removed.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the claim that no prior work systematically analyzes class-wise relations with explicit acknowledgment of neighborhood-label and compatibility-matrix approaches. It adds positioning against graph kernels, prototype classifiers, label-structure methods, and transformers. Energy-landscape and structural-balance references disappear, substantially changing the claimed intellectual foundation.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, abstract, introduction, and contextual-embedding explanation are extensively rewritten. The energy-landscape section and structural-balance appendix are removed, GNN-integration details move into the main experiments, and the appendices are reorganized. Broader-impact and acknowledgment sections are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation, with substantial resizing and relocation of displays. Learning curves are redrawn, the integration table expands, average-gap columns and new benchmark/sensitivity tables appear, and a training-size plot is added. The Squirrel matrix display and structural-balance diagram are removed.

improvement.justification: Broader benchmarking, targeted sensitivity tests, and more explicit acknowledgment of prior work improve empirical coverage and positioning. However, v2 removes the strong ALT-APPNP comparison and introduces unsupported interpretations: Remark A.5 says combined features consistently perform best despite contrary Cornell and Wisconsin results in Table 7, while Appendix B.4 claims robustness to landmark quantity without testing that quantity. These benefits and losses in evidential reliability prevent a confident net quality judgment.
